title: 3.6.13 Lab: Nested-Structure Mutation
description: Show that a spread copy is only one level deep: change a nested array inside the copy and the original still changes. Then fix it with a deep copy. Auto-graded.

steps.title: Copy the outer object with spread
steps.instructions: Create an object (the lesson calls it student; name it for what you are building) that contains a nested array called scores (for example, scores: [90, 85]). Make a shallow copy called shallow with the object spread syntax: a new object with the same keys.

steps.title: Change the nested array inside the copy
steps.instructions: Push a new value into the nested array of shallow. Then log both shallow and student. Notice student changed too, because a shallow copy still shares the nested array.

steps.title: Make a deep copy instead
steps.instructions: Use structuredClone to make a copy (the lesson calls it deep; any name works) that goes all the way down. Push a DIFFERENT value into the nested array of deep, then log both again to prove student is now untouched. Make the deep copy with structuredClone; that is what this lab is about.

requirements.title: outer object copied with spread
requirements.description: Code copies an object with the spread syntax. Help: 3.6.10 (Defensive Copying: [...] and {...})
requirements.hint: Make a copy with spread in braces. It is a new object, but anything nested inside is still shared.

requirements.title: nested array pushed into
requirements.description: Code pushes a value into the nested array. Help: 3.6.9 (Side Effects and Copies)
requirements.hint: Push into the nested array: reach it through the copy (shallow.scores) and call .push on it.

requirements.title: deep made with structuredClone
requirements.description: Code makes deep by calling structuredClone. Help: 3.6.9 (Side Effects and Copies)
requirements.hint: Assign the deep copy with structuredClone: const deep = structuredClone(student);

requirements.title: objects logged
requirements.description: Code calls console.log. Help: 3.6.9 (Side Effects and Copies)
requirements.hint: Log the copy and the original after each change, so you can see whether the original moved.

requirements.title: the shallow copy shares the nested array, the deep copy does not
requirements.description: shallow.scores matches student.scores (they are the same array), deep.scores is different from it, and the output shows the arrays. Help: 3.6.9 (Side Effects and Copies)
requirements.hint: Push into shallow.scores and student.scores changes too. Push a different number into deep.scores and student.scores stays as it was.

checks.fail: Make student (with a scores array), a spread copy called shallow and a structuredClone copy called deep. After pushing into each copy, the shallow copy matches student (they share the array) and the deep copy differs.
Print the arrays after each change, at least four lines, so the output shows what moved.

requirements.title: the arrays are printed by code that runs
requirements.description: Console.log calls that run print the arrays held by student, shallow and deep. Help: 3.6.9 (Side Effects and Copies)
requirements.hint: Print the caller's data with a console.log that runs. Typed-in text, or a print that never runs, does not count.

checks.fail: Print the arrays after each change with console.log calls that run, at least three prints; typed text does not count.
